outcome: No accepted proof, counterexample or formal verification of Schinzel's hypothesis H over Z has been found since 26 January 2024; the only in-window claims that would settle it are three single-author, non-peer-reviewed Preprints.org papers by Huan Xiao (H in May/June 2025, Bateman-Horn in December 2025), which I could not open and which show no public engagement, while the in-window work I could open (Behajaina, Debes and Konig, arXiv 2502.09959) treats the integer case as open.
problem_asks: (1) For every finite collection f1,...,fk (any k >= 1, any degrees) of nonconstant irreducible polynomials with integer coefficients and positive leading coefficients. (2) For each such collection, the disjunction holds: either (2a) there are infinitely many positive integers n for which f1(n),...,fk(n) are all prime, or (2b) there is a fixed integer m > 1 such that, for every n, m divides some f_i(n). The statement asserts this for every collection, so establishing it for a collection requires (2a) whenever (2b) fails for that collection. Examples the statement contains: twin primes (k=2, f1=n, f2=n+2), Bunyakovsky's conjecture (k=1), and Dickson's prime k-tuples (k linear polynomials).

events.what_happened: Chun-xuan Jiang, 'Proof of Schinzel's Hypothesis', Algebras Groups and Geometries 18 (2001), pp. 1-10 (Hadronic Press). The author attribution and the content summary come from a search-result summary of a CiteSeerX copy of the PDF; the PDF itself could not be opened (the CiteSeerX link redirects to a web-archive copy that the fetch tool refused). The summary says the paper's arithmetic-function method also yields finite Fermat, Mersenne, repunit, Santilli and Weiss primes.
events.delivers: As titled, a claimed full proof of Schinzel's Hypothesis H over Z. Not checked: the argument could not be read, so whether it covers every collection, or only some, is unknown.
events.remains: Nothing, if the claim were correct. The later sources I read (Bodin, Debes and Najib 2019/2020; Skorobogatov and Sofos 2020/2023; the Wikipedia article) all treat H as open, and none cites Jiang's paper as a proof (reference lists not read in full).
events.time_since_posted: about 25 years; no review found in searches (zbMATH/MathSciNet not reached)
events.doubts: (1) Every later source I read treats H as open, including the 2023 Inventiones paper that is the main partial result; a full proof would be expected to be cited there, and I did not find it cited. (2) Secondary sources, weak and unverified (a Chinese site reproducing a 2007 article, and a Douban blog post), describe the same author's claimed disproofs and proofs in the same journal as not taken up by the mathematical community, and quote a reply from a Yale mathematician calling such notes very difficult to read. (3) No review of this paper was reached.
events.direction: Claims that H holds for all collections, so it cuts in favour of H; if accepted it would settle H in full.

events.what_happened: Alexei N. Skorobogatov and Efthymios Sofos, 'Schinzel Hypothesis on average and rational points', arXiv:2005.02998 (v1 6 May 2020; v3 4 Sep 2022). Published in Inventiones Mathematicae 231(2) (2023) 673-739, DOI 10.1007/s00222-022-01153-6. The abstract (opened) says they 'resolve Schinzel's Hypothesis (H) for 100% of polynomials of arbitrary degree', and deduce that a positive proportion of diagonal conic bundles over Q with any given number of degenerate fibres have a rational point. Published-PDF dates (search snippet): received 7 Nov 2020, accepted 18 Aug 2022, published online 28 Sep 2022.
events.revisions: v1 6 May 2020; v3 4 Sep 2022 (per arXiv abs page, opened); journal version Inventiones Mathematicae 231(2), 2023.
events.delivers: H holds for 100% of tuples of polynomials of given degrees when ordered by height (a density statement: for almost every tuple, not for each tuple). The paper's Theorem 1.1, as quoted in a search snippet (not read in the paper), is the single-polynomial analogue: for 100% of Bouniakowsky polynomials of degree d there is a natural number m with P(m) prime. The fixed-divisor side is not addressed.
events.remains: H for each individual collection, including the exceptional set of tuples of density zero, and the degree-1 multi-polynomial case over Z (Dickson's prime k-tuples), which a density result does not reach.

checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted for publication 18 Aug 2022; published online 28 Sep 2022 (dates from the published PDF, via a search snippet; the Springer page itself was not opened)

events.time_since_posted: about 6.4 years since arXiv v1; about 3 years since journal acceptance
events.direction: Supports H in the density sense (almost every tuple satisfies it). It neither proves H for each collection nor disproves it.

events.what_happened: Skorobogatov and Sofos, 'Generic diagonal conic bundles revisited', arXiv:2212.14778 (v1 30 Dec 2022; v2 3 Jan 2024). Abstract (v2, opened): 'Schinzel's Hypothesis holds for 100% of n-tuples of integer polynomials' satisfying the usual necessary conditions, with the primes subject to extra constraints: Legendre symbol conditions, a fixed residue class of m modulo M, and size bounds (min P_i(m) > |P|(log|P|)^(eps/2) and m at most (log|P|)^(n+eps)). The 'usual necessary conditions' are the no-local-obstruction conditions (for every prime l, the product is not divisible by t^l - t mod l). Published in Quarterly Journal of Mathematics 75(3) (2024) 835-849, DOI 10.1093/qmath/haae022, online 14 June 2024 (search snippet of the Glasgow repository).
events.revisions: v1 30 Dec 2022 (whether v1 already contains the Legendre/size refinement was not checked); v2 3 Jan 2024 (opened; contains it); QJM 75(3), 2024. If the refinement first appeared in v2, the date would be 2024-01-03, still before 26 Jan 2024.
events.delivers: H holds for 100% of n-tuples satisfying the no-local-obstruction condition (density by height), with the primes additionally in a prescribed residue class mod M, with prescribed Legendre symbols between values, and with explicit size bounds. A density result in the same sense as 2005.02998; the refinement concerns constraints on m, not coverage of every collection.
events.remains: H for every individual collection; the density-zero exceptional set; the fixed-divisor alternative is not affected.

checked_by.who: Quarterly Journal of Mathematics (Oxford) editorial process (referees not named in any source read)
checked_by.what_they_did: Published, QJM 75(3), 2024, per the Glasgow repository record (search snippet; not opened)

events.direction: Supports H in the density sense, with extra prime constraints. Neither disproves H nor settles it for each collection.

events.what_happened: Bodin, Debes and Najib, 'The Schinzel Hypothesis for Polynomials', arXiv:1902.08155 (February 2019); Transactions of the AMS 373 (2020) 12 (per search snippet). Proves Schinzel's hypothesis for a wide class of polynomial rings in place of Z (polynomials in at least one variable over Z; polynomials in several variables over an arbitrary field), via a version of the Hilbert specialization property over rings. Not opened: the arXiv page and the PDF were not fetched; the description is from search summaries.
events.delivers: Polynomial-ring analogue of H: Z replaced by a polynomial ring (e.g. Z[T]), 'prime' by 'irreducible'. Not H over Z.
events.remains: H over Z, for every collection and every degree (the problem as stated).

checked_by.who: Transactions of the American Mathematical Society (refereed)
checked_by.what_they_did: Published, Trans. AMS 373 (2020) 12 (per search result listing; not opened)

events.direction: Analogue: cuts toward H in the polynomial-ring setting only. Does not bear on H over Z.

events.what_happened: Lior Bary-Soroker, 'Irreducible values of polynomials', arXiv:1005.4528 (May 2010); Advances in Mathematics 2012 (per search snippet). Arithmetic analogue of H over pseudo algebraically closed fields, with a quantitative form. Not opened: described from search summaries only.
events.delivers: Analogue over pseudo algebraically closed fields (and a quantitative version); not H over Z.
events.remains: H over Z, for every collection (the problem as stated).
events.direction: Analogue: does not bear on H over Z.

events.what_happened: Wataru Kai, 'Linear patterns of prime elements in number fields', arXiv:2306.16983 (v1 29 June 2023; v5 12 March 2026). Abstract (opened): 'We prove a number field analogue of the Green-Tao-Ziegler theorem on simultaneous prime values of degree 1 polynomials', with pairwise linearly independent linear parts.
events.revisions: v1 29 Jun 2023; v5 12 Mar 2026 (per arXiv abs page, opened).
events.delivers: Simultaneous prime elements for degree-1 polynomials in the ring of integers of a number field, with pairwise linearly independent linear parts. Degree 1 only, and over number fields rather than Z. The abstract does not claim the integer case.
events.remains: H over Z for every collection, including degree-1 collections over Z (Dickson's prime k-tuples), and every collection of degree greater than 1.
events.direction: Analogue in the linear case over number fields. Does not settle H over Z; bears on it only as the linear-case analogue.

events.what_happened: Huan Xiao (affiliation given as School of Artificial Intelligence, Zhuhai City Polytechnic, China), Preprints.org, DOI 10.20944/preprints202505.0651.v2, 'From Golomb to Schinzel', posted 9 June 2025, labelled 'Not peer-reviewed version'. The abstract, as shown in search results, describes H as a conjecture on prime values of polynomials and says the author proves it by Golomb's method (keywords include the Bateman-Horn conjecture). A companion-paper snippet says the author 'recently proposed a proof of the Schinzel hypothesis by the method of Golomb, together with a contradiction argument'. The same DOI's v1 is reported in one search summary as 'A Note on the Bateman-Horn Conjecture', posted 9 May 2025, whose abstract (as summarised) sets out to investigate whether Bateman-Horn holds by Golomb's method. All Preprints.org full-text fetches returned HTTP 403; the text was not read.
events.revisions: v1 9 May 2025 (title 'A Note on the Bateman-Horn Conjecture' per one search summary, not opened); v2 9 June 2025 ('From Golomb to Schinzel', opened only via search summary). Date choice: if the H argument first appeared in v2, the date is 2025-06-09. Both are inside the window; the choice is for the later pass.
events.delivers: If the argument is correct: H over Z for all collections, both alternatives (2a) and (2b), i.e. the full statement. The abstract as shown does not state a restriction. Unverified: the argument was not readable.
events.remains: Nothing, if the claim holds. As the record stands, the whole statement is asserted and unverified.
events.time_since_posted: about 17 months since v1; about 16 months since v2; no review, comment, citation or error report found in searches
events.doubts: (1) Single author; the posting is labelled not peer-reviewed and I found no journal submission record. (2) H is a long-open problem: settling it would also yield the infinitude of twin primes and of primes n^2+1 (stated by Hindry-Rivoal's French note, as quoted in a search snippet, and by Wikipedia). No later source I read mentions this preprint. (3) Hindry and Rivoal's undated French note on Golomb's Lambda-calculus (not readable here) says that Golomb's method does not apply as elegantly to this case and must be adapted, and that beyond degree 1 H seems out of reach. This is a statement about difficulty, not a refutation, and the same snippet says Conrad adapted the method to Bateman-Horn, so the method is live. (4) I did not identify a specific error in any step, since the text could not be read. (5) The author's publication record in number theory could not be verified (sciprofiles and Mathematics Genealogy links appeared in search results and were not opened).
events.direction: Claims H holds for every collection, so it cuts in favour of H; if correct it settles the problem.

events.what_happened: Huan Xiao, 'From Golomb to Bateman-Horn', Preprints.org, DOI 10.20944/preprints202512.2666.v1, posted 31 December 2025, labelled 'Not peer-reviewed version'. Abstract (search snippet): 'The Bateman-Horn conjecture is a conjecture on prime values in polynomials. We prove it by Golomb's method.' Not opened (403).
events.delivers: As claimed: the Bateman-Horn conjecture, the quantitative form of H. Standard relation (my reading, not stated by the preprint, whose text I could not read): if the Bateman-Horn asymptotic holds, then for a collection with no fixed divisor the count of simultaneous prime values tends to infinity, so a proof of Bateman-Horn would also yield alternative (2a) of H for such collections. Unverified.
events.remains: Nothing, if the claim holds; the fixed-divisor alternative is not separately treated in the snippet.
events.time_since_posted: about 9.5 months; no engagement found in searches
events.doubts: Same as the 2025 H preprint: single author, not peer-reviewed, no engagement found. Bateman-Horn is the stronger claim and the snippet gives no step. The same author claims H, BH and Chowla in the same method within about seven months; a reader should check whether the three arguments are the same argument (not verified here).
events.direction: Claims the quantitative form of H (and hence, on the standard relation, H's infinitude alternative); cuts in favour of H if correct.

events.what_happened: Huan Xiao, 'From Bateman-Horn to Chowla', Preprints.org, DOI 10.20944/preprints202601.0277.v1, posted 5 January 2026, labelled not peer-reviewed. Abstract (search snippet): a new formula for the Liouville function, and a 'parallel proof of the Chowla conjecture' using the method behind the Bateman-Horn proof. Not opened.
events.delivers: As claimed: the Chowla conjecture for the Liouville function, a different problem. Says nothing about H.
events.doubts: Not about H. Recorded because the same author uses the same method for H, Bateman-Horn and Chowla.
events.direction: Not bearing on H (neighbouring problem, discarded for this record).

events.what_happened: Angelot Behajaina, Pierre Debes and Joachim Konig, 'Integrally Hilbertian rings and the polynomial Schinzel hypothesis', arXiv:2502.09959 (v1 14 Feb 2025; v2 8 Apr 2026). Abstract (opened): if Z is an integrally Hilbertian ring, the hypothesis holds with Z replaced by the polynomial ring Z[U] and 'prime' replaced by 'irreducible'. Theorem 1.3: a Hilbertian Krull domain is integrally Hilbertian; Corollary 1.4: rings of integers of number fields are integrally Hilbertian; Theorem 1.7: Z[Y1..Yn] is a Schinzel ring for partial-degree Weil heights. Corollary 1.10 (opened in the HTML): 'Assume that the original Schinzel Hypothesis over Z is true'; then for irreducible P1..Ps in Z[T] with no fixed divisor there exist monic M in Z[T] of arbitrary degree d >= 1 with P_i(M(t)) all prime for infinitely many t. The classical integer case is not proved in the paper.
events.revisions: v1 14 Feb 2025; v2 8 Apr 2026 (per arXiv abs page, opened).
events.delivers: Polynomial-ring analogue: H with Z replaced by Z[U1..Un] (n >= 1) and 'prime' by 'irreducible', for integrally Hilbertian base rings including rings of integers of number fields. Over Z, only the conditional Corollary 1.10 (assuming the classical hypothesis) is stated.
events.remains: H over Z for every collection, including the degree-1 multi-polynomial case over Z and every collection of degree greater than 1 (per this paper's own framing).
events.time_since_posted: about 20 months since v1; no engagement found beyond the arXiv listing
events.direction: Analogue results true as stated; for the classical integer case, neither proves nor disproves H. The conditional corollary is a reduction, not support for H.

events.what_happened: F. Amoroso, N. H. Andriamandratomanana and D. Simon, 'Sur une conjecture de Schinzel', arXiv:2502.10549 (v1 14 Feb 2025; v2 22 Jun 2025), in French. Abstract (opened): a new proof, with explicit bounds, of a Schinzel conjecture on the intersection of a codimension >= 2 subvariety of a power of the multiplicative group with a one-dimensional torus. This is Schinzel's 1965 conjecture on coprime polynomials, not H.
events.revisions: v1 14 Feb 2025; v2 22 Jun 2025 (per arXiv abs page, opened).
events.delivers: A different Schinzel conjecture (1965, subvarieties of tori / coprime polynomials): explicit proof. Says nothing about prime values of polynomials.
events.direction: Unrelated to H (namesake). Recorded and discarded.

events.what_happened: Giacomo Bortolussi, 'Worse than square-root cancellation in Bateman-Horn's conjecture', arXiv:2604.02287 (v1 2 Apr 2026; v2 23 Jun 2026). events.revisions: v1 2 Apr 2026; v2 23 Jun 2026 (per arXiv abs page, opened).
events.delivers: An averaged result on the error term of Bateman-Horn; does not prove BH or H as such.
events.direction: Neighbouring problem (Bateman-Horn error term, averaged). Does not bear on H's statement. Discarded for this record.

summary: As far as I could establish, Schinzel's hypothesis H over Z is still open at the time of this record. No accepted proof, counterexample or formal verification turned up in about 45 searches, and the most recent substantive paper I could open (Behajaina, Debes and Konig, arXiv 2502.09959, v2 April 2026) treats the integer case as open, offering only a conditional corollary. Within the window, the only claims that would settle H in full are three single-author, non-peer-reviewed Preprints.org papers by Huan Xiao: 'From Golomb to Schinzel' (DOI 202505.0651.v2, 9 June 2025, whose v1 of 9 May 2025 is reported under the title 'A Note on the Bateman-Horn Conjecture'), 'From Golomb to Bateman-Horn' (31 December 2025), and 'From Bateman-Horn to Chowla' (5 January 2026, a different problem). None of the Preprints.org PDFs could be opened (all returned 403), so the claims are known only from abstract snippets and search summaries, and I found no review, citation, comment or error report for any of them. Pre-window events: Skorobogatov and Sofos (arXiv May 2020; Inventiones 2023) prove H for 100% of polynomial tuples in the height-density sense, and their arXiv v2 (3 January 2024; QJM 2024) strengthens this with Legendre-symbol and size constraints on the primes; this is a refereed density result, not a proof for each collection. Chun-xuan Jiang's 'Proof of Schinzel's Hypothesis' (Algebras Groups and Geometries 18, 2001) claims a full proof, but I could not read it and found no review; later sources treat H as open. The analogues (Bodin, Debes and Najib 2019 for polynomial rings; Bary-Soroker 2010; Kai 2023 for linear patterns in number fields) answer different questions. Namesakes (Amoroso et al. 2025 on Schinzel's 1965 coprime-polynomial conjecture; Zannier; Dimitrov on Schinzel-Zassenhaus; Sierpinski's Hypothesis H1 of Dec 2025) bear on nothing here. Wikipedia's cached page (dated by the fetch tool 7 Oct 2026) still lists H as open, cites only Skorobogatov and Sofos as recent progress, and does not mention AI. AI: no source I read names an AI system in connection with H. The openai/math repository (719 manuscripts in 372 families, 'produced by an internal OpenAI model') shows no family on H, prime values of polynomials or Bateman-Horn in the slices I could read (see incomplete for the gap). The Erdos-problem AI results, AlphaEvolve and Gemini Deep Think work I found do not touch H. Whether Xiao used AI tools cannot be determined from the material I could reach; the author's affiliation is a 'School of Artificial Intelligence', which is an affiliation, not evidence of AI involvement. Close calls: (a) whether the H argument first appeared in v1 (9 May 2025) or v2 (9 June 2025) of Xiao's DOI, both inside the window; (b) whether the 2001 Jiang claim counts as an event at all, which I record because it claims the whole result; (c) whether the Skorobogatov-Sofos density theorem counts as H 'in relation to the problem', given that the statement asks about every collection.
competing_reading: That Xiao's three preprints contain a genuine proof that has not yet been read by specialists. The method is live (Hindry and Rivoal's note says Conrad adapted Golomb's method to Bateman-Horn), and the French note only says the method does not apply elegantly to H and must be adapted, which is a claim about difficulty rather than impossibility. Against this: settling H would also give the infinitude of twin primes, so a short single-author argument would normally draw immediate scrutiny, and in roughly 16 to 17 months I found no visible uptake, citation or error report. Against the Skorobogatov-Sofos reading as a partial result: the density statement is not the statement asked for, so it should not be counted as resolving H for any given collection. For the Jiang 2001 paper: it could be a neglected argument; I could not read it, so this rests entirely on the absence of review and later citation.
what_would_settle_it: A referee report or journal decision on Xiao's H paper; a zbMATH or MathSciNet review of Jiang (2001) and of the Xiao preprints; the Preprints.org full texts with version history and any AI or tool declaration; a specific error identified in the key Golomb-method step, or a confirmation of it, by a number theorist; a Lean or Coq formalisation of the Xiao argument with no sorry; or a later paper that cites Xiao and treats H as settled or refuted.
